newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks end firm, setting new 1996 high.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks end firm, setting new 1996 high.

text.p: Argentine stocks pushed higher in token turnover Tuesday to post their second consecutive record high for 1996.
Traders said the market rose on residual momentum from its recent rally and on fresh gains on Wall Street Tuesday.
"It was a dead market today, but the tone is very firm," one trader said.
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV rose 0.6 percent to 642.11, extending gains so far this week to 2.2 percent.

Floor volume shrank to 6.3 million pesos in the session, which ended three hours early, compared to an already weak tally of 23 million pesos Monday. Over-the-counter deals totaled 39.4 million pesos against 117 million Monday.

Brokers forecast turnover would remain tight when trading resumes Thursday due to the general strike called for that day by the trade unions, which are protesting recent presidential decrees on labor reforms.
"We're not really worried about the effects of the strike from a political or economic standpoint, but it's likely to extend the market trading lull," another dealer said.
Technical analysts said the MerVal might pull back gently Thursday and Friday, forecasting a near-term floor of 630.
The broad market index rose 0.1 percent Tuesday, with winners beating losers 25 to five and 13 issues closing flat.
Top blue-chip performers were petrochemical concern Ipako, steelmaker Siderca and foods giant Molinos, which advanced 4.5 percent, 2.9 percent and 1.4 percent, respectively.
The only decliners were real estate developer Irsa, off 0.9 percent, and Telecom and Telefnica, down 0.5 percent and 0.2 percent, respectively, on profit-taking after recent hefty gains.
